rationale: Execute the admitted transfer-target question: a four-voter in-memory cluster in which one non-leader member is demoted with DemoteVoter, then LeadershipTransferToServer names that non-voter; the control repeats the same setup without the demotion. Four comparisons test the documented graceful-failure promise and whether the named target actually gains leadership. Native feedback showed the control transferring to the voter and the non-voter case returning without error while another member led, but only the retained execution is cited later.

scope.description: Two leadership-transfer invocations on real four-voter in-memory clusters. In both, a non-leader member is chosen as the explicit target; in the trigger case that member is first demoted to non-voter through the public DemoteVoter API and the committed configuration is allowed to reach it, while the control keeps it a voter. Each case records the transfer future's outcome, whether the named target ever reported Leader, whether the final leader is the target, a sampled leaderless interval and the members' terms after the attempt.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms), so a new election can complete quickly.
The demotion is committed before the transfer is requested; the harness waits 200 ms and does not assert configuration convergence separately.

The leaderless interval is estimated from repeated 10 ms sampling whose measured effective rate was about one sample per 116 ms (43 samples), so a shorter leaderless gap can be missed and a zero count is not evidence of absence.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about the effect on client requests accepted during the transfer window, and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely (rejected earlier by the replState lookup) are not exercised.

experiment.prefix: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with four bootstrapped voters, waits for c.Leader(), and selects the first non-leader raft as the target. The trigger calls leader.DemoteVoter(targetID, 0, 5s) and sleeps 200 ms; the control skips demotion. The case event records the target role, its term before, and the watch parameters. The harness then calls leader.LeadershipTransferToServer(targetID, target.localAddr) and records the future's error and duration, samples target.State() and c.Leader() every 10 ms for the watch window, and emits a result event with future_ok, future_error, future_ms, target_ever_leader, final_leader_is_target, no_leader_ms_sampled, samples, target_term_after and other_member_term_max_after.
experiment.responsibility: The library documents that a leadership transfer makes the target up to date, sends TimeoutNow, and that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. Choosing which targets are admissible, and reporting an outcome that matches what happened to authority, are therefore library responsibilities: the caller supplies a member id that the configuration itself currently marks as a non-voter.

comparisons.description: Control: a transfer to a voter must install that voter as leader.
Control: a transfer that installs the named voter must complete without error.
A transfer to a member the configuration marks as a non-voter cannot be promoted, so the documented graceful failure requires an error; a successful future contradicts it.
If the transfer is admitted as successful, the named target must hold leadership; a target that never leads contradicts the transfer's stated purpose.
